item: The airplane guard patches a real call written back over it; the dns tests install it first; the test hook names a guard removed while flagged installed
summary: airplane._installed could be True while socket.getaddrinfo held the stdlib's own function: every test in tests/test_dns_proxy_guard.py records the real getaddrinfo with monkeypatch BEFORE the process's first fetch installs the guard over the stand-in, and the undo writes the real call back over the guard. install_airplane_socket_guard() then returned early at 'if _installed' and could not repair it, so airplane mode let DNS through and tests/test_egress_window.py::test_with_no_window_airplane_still_refuses_before_any_real_socket_call reached the real resolver when the two ran in one worker (3 of 3 runs of the 120 files that touch the socket calls under -n 4, on a clean main too; it passed in the full suite by order luck). Fix: _install_patches, when already installed, patches again any call that holds a real function (the saved _orig_* or the stdlib's own, kept in _REAL_AT_IMPORT because tests swap _orig_* for spies) and leaves a deliberate stand-in alone; removed_while_installed() is the shared reader. The dns tests install the connect guard before they patch. tests/conftest.py's hook also names a test that leaves the guard removed while flagged installed (patches it again, fails that one test), and imports the airplane module at the first test's setup: run alone, the first fetch used to import it inside a monkeypatch window and airplane captured the test's stand-in as the real _orig_getaddrinfo for the process (measured). Red without: 2 of 3 new tests fail without the heal; the first dns test fails by name without the fixture. 120 socket files under -n 4: 4,727 passed (egress-window green); full -n 4 suite 24,418 passed, 1 failed (the local-only gzip test).
